Questions

Before you call

Straight answers to what North Florida homeowners ask us most — about demolition, hauling and tarping alike. First Coast Haul connects you with local partner crews — your estimate and the work itself are handled by the contractor matched to your job.

How much does a job cost?+

It depends on the size and type of job, so we price it in person. Book a free on-site estimate anywhere in our Jacksonville and North Florida service area — the crew looks at the work, gives you the price before anything starts, and there's no obligation if you pass.

How soon can you get here?+

Junk pickup is same day when we have an opening, otherwise the next day we can get there — call or text early in the day for the best shot. Emergency roof tarping after a storm is dispatched as fast as conditions safely allow, and demolition is scheduled at your free estimate.

Do you handle permits and utility shutoffs for demolition?+

The crew matched to your job walks you through what's needed at the free estimate — permit requirements vary by city and by the size of the structure — and work doesn't start until utilities are confirmed off and the plan is agreed.

What happens to the debris after a demolition?+

It's part of the job: the crew tears it out, loads it and hauls it away in the same visit, and the site is left clear and swept. Concrete, metal and clean wood are recycled where local facilities take them; the rest goes to licensed disposal.

Can you tear out just one room?+

Yes — interior demolition is usually exactly that: a kitchen, a bathroom, flooring, a wall or a whole interior gut before a remodel. Tell us the scope when you book and the crew prices just that work at the estimate.

Will you take just one junk item?+

Yes. One couch, one mattress or one appliance is a normal job for us — you don't need a full load to book.

Do I have to move everything to the curb first?+

No. Crews load it from wherever it sits. Just tell us about stairs, tight doorways or a long carry when you book, and we'll plan for it at the estimate.

Do you do whole-house and estate cleanouts?+

Yes — one room, the garage, or the whole house. We handle estate, foreclosure and move-out cleanouts for families, landlords and realtors, and leave the space broom-clean.

My roof is leaking after a storm. How fast can you tarp it?+

Call or text as soon as it's safe — storm tarping is the emergency service, and crews are dispatched across North Florida as conditions allow. A heavy-duty tarp, secured with battens, stops the water so a leak doesn't turn into ceiling, insulation and mold damage while you line up permanent repairs.

Is tarping a permanent fix?+

No — a tarp is temporary protection, meant to keep water out for days to weeks while permanent roof repairs are scheduled. Your crew will tell you honestly what the roof needs next.

What don't you haul?+

Paint, chemicals and fuel have to go to the county hazardous waste drop-off, so set those aside and tell us about them when you book. Just about everything else — furniture, appliances, concrete, dirt, yard and construction debris — is on our list.

Where do you work?+

Across North Florida: Jacksonville and the Beaches, Orange Park, Fleming Island, Middleburg, Green Cove Springs, St. Augustine, Palm Coast, Palatka, Fernandina Beach, Yulee, Macclenny, Starke and Lake City. If you're nearby, text your ZIP and we'll tell you if we can get there.

Roof Tarping + Storm Response in North Florida

North Florida roofs take the weather first — hurricanes, tropical storms, nor'easters and plain summer downpours. First Coast Haul dispatches local crews to get a heavy-duty tarp secured over the damage fast, document it with photos, and clear the debris that's in the way — buying you dry time to line up permanent repairs.

Questions

Roof tarping questions

How long will a secured tarp hold?+

A batten-secured heavy-duty tarp typically holds through weeks of Florida rain and wind. Loose-laid tarps are the ones that end up in the neighbor's yard — which is why ours are fastened down.

Do you work with my insurance claim?+

The crew photographs the damage and the finished tarp and gives you the photos for your records — most homeowners file them with their claim. We don't bill your insurer directly; you pay the crew and keep the documentation.

Concrete Removal in Jacksonville & North Florida

North Florida's tree roots and sandy soil are rough on concrete: driveways heave and crack, patios tilt, and old slabs sit exactly where the new project needs to go. Our crews break up and remove driveways, slabs, patios and sidewalks, cut rebar and mesh, and haul every chunk away — most loads go to concrete recycling where local facilities take them. Whether you're re-pouring, extending a driveway or clearing a lot in Jacksonville or anywhere on the First Coast, it starts with a free on-site estimate.

  • Rebar and wire mesh cut and hauled with the load
